relationship.direction: peatland rewetting is targeted where artificial DRAINAGE (canal) DENSITY IS HIGH — peatlands receiving dams averaged 2.5 km km-2, about twice the 1.2 km km-2 of all peatlands; dense canals are what make a peatland both degraded and restorable, so the variable selects the intervention zone rather than excluding it

hydrological potential for paludiculture on rewetted peat is HIGH where the mean lowest groundwater level sits 0-30 cm below the surface, moderate at 30-80 cm and marginal at 80-160 cm — the shallower the dry-season water table, the more rewettable the land

UPWARD seepage (below -0.1 mm/d) gives the highest potential because groundwater feeds the root zone; neutral seepage is moderate and downward seepage up to 0.5 mm/d marginal — land losing water downward is hard to keep wet
